item.title: The UK FCA says it plans to require DeFi platforms to obtain authorization, adopting a stricter stance than the US and the EU after the $6.3B Binance hack (Financial Times)
item.description: The UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), led by Jane Moore (Head of Payments and Digital Assets), plans to mandate authorization for DeFi platforms to close regulatory gaps in anti-money laundering and consumer protection. Regulators emphasize that the recent $6.3 billion Binance hack, where stolen assets flowed through DeFi protocols for laundering, necessitates stricter oversight beyond current market norms.

item.title: OpenAI says it corrected a GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol launch billing mistake that had incorrectly discounted usage; Astra users will now hit their limits 40% faster (Graham Barlow/TechRadar)
item.description: If you've been enjoying using OpenAI's new GPT-6.2 models over the past week, especially since they also now work in Chat mode, I've got some bad news: OpenAI has admitted that it made a billing mistake when launching the models — and now that it's corrected the error, you'll reach your usage limits much faster. item.title: Netherlands Plans to Fight Rollout of Proposed US Curbs on ASML
item.description: The Dutch government said it will resist US plans to further restrict ASML Holding NV's sales to China, calling the proposed rules a threat to Europe's most valuable company.

item.title: VC investors dump old funds at steep discounts to chase AI riches
item.description: Pension funds and endowments ditch legacy stakes at knockdown prices to free up cash for next-generation tech start-ups

item.title: X rolls out its first parental controls for users aged 13 to 17, defaulting teens to protected mode, restricting sensitive media, and disabling targeted ads (Steve Dent/Engadget)
item.description: X has launched parental control features for users aged 13-17, defaulting accounts to protected modes with restricted sensitive media and targeted ads. Guardians can now manage follower requests, set time limits, and filter content, a move primarily aimed at mitigating global regulatory risks regarding minor safety on digital platforms.

item.title: ASML’s CEO makes the case for selling chips to China
item.description: ASML CEO Christophe Fouquet argued that export controls should target only the most advanced technology rather than a total blockade. He warned that over-restricting China forces domestic acceleration in chip development, whereas maintaining a 'generation gap' via older equipment exports keeps Beijing tethered to Western hardware ecosystems.

item.title: Microsoft details how state-backed hackers use the ARTEX AI framework to automate cyberattacks
item.description: Microsoft Threat Intelligence reported that the AI penetration-testing framework ARTEX is being exploited by state-backed groups, including Salt Typhoon and Crystal Typhoon. The framework uses a multi-agent architecture to automate the entire attack lifecycle, significantly lowering the barrier for complex breaches against sensitive infrastructure and agencies.

item.title: Nvidia halts server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia after tighter US export controls
item.description: Nvidia has directed partners to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia in response to tightened US BIS export controls. The move aims to prevent Chinese companies from bypassing sanctions via third-country cloud providers, triggering market volatility for B300 chips and imposing strict end-user compliance reviews for regional data centers.

Moonshot AI expects the gap between major releases could grow from six months to a year or longer if it loses access to overseas computing power, people familiar with the matter said. item.title: Meta Refused to Share Muse for Testing, UK Financial Watchdog Complains
item.description: Meta declined a joint-testing request from Colin Payne, head of innovation at the UK's Financial Conduct Authority (FCA), regarding its Muse AI assistant. The FCA is concerned about potential consumer harm in autonomous financial interactions, particularly as Muse integrates with major British retailers.

item.title: Musk Says Every US Kid to Get Two SpaceX Shares, Doubling Pledge
item.description: Elon Musk announced on X that he will grant two SpaceX shares to every child under 18 in the United States. One share will be transferred by SpaceX next month, and the other by Musk personally in June, as part of his vision for multiplanetary goals.

item.title: The next generation of bionic hands is here—and they can feel
item.description: Avi Davidson lost his left hand as a teenager. Since then, he’s cycled through a few prosthetics. But his latest is different—it’s wired up to nerves in the upper part of his forearm and allows him to feel pressure. For the first time in years, he can use his left limb to handle delicate objects like grapes, eggs, and a loved one’s hand. item.title: Confidential Data Sent to Chinese AI Firm MiniMax Was Accessed Without Authorization, US Research Firm Identifies
item.description: Dragos Chief Research Officer HD Moore revealed that AI startup MiniMax improperly stores private web links from user prompts despite opt-out requests. Security researchers observed unauthorized third-party access to these links, accompanied by suspicious traffic originating from Beijing, Shanghai, and the Moscow region, alongside attempts to exfiltrate private software code.

item.title: The Global Memory-Chip Shortage Will Cost Us All
item.description: Global memory chip supplies are tightening as tech giants like Google, Microsoft, and Meta aggressively procure RAM for AI data center expansion. This shift has triggered a surge in consumer electronic manufacturing costs, with industry experts projecting significant retail price hikes and supply constraints lasting through 2027.

item.title: Software stocks spared in tech rout as AI narrative shifts
item.description: Investors are rotating away from semiconductor dominance toward software firms possessing proprietary datasets and entrenched customer bases. Despite early 2026 sell-offs driven by fears of AI-driven obsolescence, the software sector now exhibits greater defensive value amidst broader tech market volatility.

item.title: Microsoft says state-backed hacking groups in China and North Korea, including Salt Typhoon, have added AI penetration testing tool ARTEX to their arsenals (Jonathan Greig/The Record)
item.description: Microsoft reports that state-sponsored hacking groups, including Salt Typhoon, have integrated the AI-powered penetration testing tool ARTEX into their offensive arsenals. By automating reconnaissance, credential theft, and vulnerability scanning, the tool compresses intrusion cycles to minutes while bypassing static signature detection via behavioral obfuscation.

item.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
item.description: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia to comply with new US export control regulations. This measure targets the loophole allowing Chinese AI developers to access restricted high-end GPU compute via local cloud providers, as firms struggle with the lack of specific compliance guidelines.

item.title: Nvidia halts chip shipments to south-east Asia
item.description: Nvidia has instructed manufacturing partners, including Dell and Supermicro, to halt server shipments containing advanced AI chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and Indonesia. This move aims to align with US Department of Commerce directives targeting cloud-based workarounds by Chinese entities and to ensure strict export control compliance.

item.title: Shein’s Slow India Start Lays Bare Limits of Billionaire Ambani’s Retail Might
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. is struggling to gain traction in its return to the Indian market through a local partnership, hampered by supply chain bottlenecks and leadership instability. The platform has yet to replicate the proprietary technological edge that propelled its global operational efficiency.

item.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness Tells Investors It Lost 65% in Third Quarter
item.description: Situational Awareness, a hedge fund founded by Leopold Aschenbrenner, reported a 65% net loss for Q3 following a liquidity crisis triggered by aggressive leveraged bets on the AI sector in July. The fund, which was forced to sell a significant portion of its public equity portfolio to Citadel to stave off implosion, is now pivoting toward more conservative risk management.

item.title: Inside Trump's effort to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO
item.description: President Trump and VP Vance engaged with Nvidia's board and counsel to confirm Jensen Huang is not a target of DOJ investigations and poses no national security risks, facilitating his reinstatement as CEO. This intervention aimed to stabilize Nvidia's share price and secure the strategic continuity of a cornerstone in the U.S. AI supply chain.

item.title: OpenAI says heavy ChatGPT users may hit limits sooner as it merges Chat and Work
item.description: OpenAI has started rolling out a unified Chat and Work experience in ChatGPT to a few of its users, amid criticism from some subscribers that the merger could restrict their usage. The ChatGPT maker began introducing the update to a small group of Pro subscribers, product lead Thibault “Tibo” Sottiaux said in a post on X on Tuesday. The rollout follows OpenAI’s earlier announcement of the merger in an email to users. An OpenAI spokesperson told TechCrunch that while most users are not expected

item.title: 2 California companies are buying Nvidia's most advanced chips. Those companies are actually Chinese-owned, a CBS News investigation reveals.
item.description: Investigations reveal that several California-based NVIDIA partners are effectively controlled by Chinese firms, with executives linked to Chinese military institutions and blacklisted entities. These entities leverage their U.S. registration to procure high-end AI chips and circumvent export controls by rerouting hardware to China via third-party jurisdictions.

item.title: Apple removes MiniMax's chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide over sexual content, after outlets showed it evidence of AI characters sexualizing children (TBIJ)
item.description: Apple has removed the AI roleplay app Talkie, developed by Shanghai-based MiniMax, from the global App Store. The move follows investigations revealing that the platform's AI characters engaged minors in psychologically damaging, harassing, and sexually suggestive roleplays, violating safety policies regarding minor protection.

item.title: Neuralink Gets Clearance for Brain-Implant Trial in ALS Patients
item.description: Neuralink has secured FDA clearance to initiate the 'LINK' pivotal study, evaluating the safety and performance of the N1 brain implant in patients with ALS. The trial will utilize the R1 surgical robot to implant ultra-thin threads, focusing on the system's ability to translate neural activity into precise digital pointer control and interface clicks.

item.title: Amazon loses its latest attempt to get out of handling more recall notices
item.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland ruled that Amazon acts as a distributor, not merely a logistics provider, regarding its 'Fulfilled by Amazon' services. Consequently, the company is mandated to comply with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission's order to recall over 400,000 hazardous third-party products, including faulty carbon monoxide detectors and non-compliant children's apparel.

item.title: Character.AI’s plan to auction off users’ private chats challenged by state AGs
item.description: Character.ai, currently under Chapter 11 bankruptcy, intends to auction sensitive data from 21 million users, including 2.1 million minors, to Smirks and Pangs Acquisition LLC. A coalition of 42 state attorneys general, led by California AG Rob Bonta and Connecticut AG William Tong, is challenging this move, citing breaches of privacy commitments and potential violations of state chatbot safety laws effective January 2027.
